programmes.d: The disappearance of a mail-order bride is suspicious when police learn of the husband's past wives.
In 1991, when the wife of a serviceman was brutally murdered in the Philippines, investigators had to reassemble a tiny computer disk that had been cut to pieces in order to find the killer.
A jeweler's search through old sales records helps police find likely suspects in a couple's murder.
When a young fireman died from what appeared to be serious but undiagnosed heart disease, his family and friends had no proof of foul play.
Garbage bag leads to a killer.
While investigating the murder of 9-year-old Jessica Knott, police use a garbage bag to connect suspect James Edward Crow, Jr. to the crime.
An investigation into the murder of Katie Poirier is stymied by the lack of a body.
In 1969, 25-year-old phone operator Diane Maxwell was raped and murdered. Her brother promised he'd find out who was responsible and bring the killer to justice.
The sensitive nose of a forensic examiner sniffs out murder.
In 1987, a human skull and some bones were discovered at a Boy Scout Camp near Farmington, Missouri. Facial reconstruction aids the investigators in this case.
An assailant avoids the law for 16 years due to a lack of evidence.

Nancy Newman and her two daughters are found brutally murdered. The crime scene has no shortage of evidence, but investigators cannot find a conclusive link to their prime suspect. To solve the puzzle, an FBI analyst designs a unique experiment.
The only clue recovered from a shooting is a twelve-guage shotgun.

A man tells police he shot an intruder who had attacked and murdered his wife. The husband paints a tragic picture and is dubbed a hero. Four years later, forensic evidence leads police to re-examine the motives of this so-called hero.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause the deaths of three people.

The body of a young woman was found a mile from her abandoned car. Police were especially concerned when they realized the victim had come to them for protection just two weeks earlier after a road rage incident.
Computers aid the police and FBI in solving a string of crimes in St. Louis.
When the number and volume of bloodstains at the scene was greater than usual, it was up to forensic scientists to find out why.
Using an anonymous letter and geographical profiling, investigators close in on a serial rapist.
When a car was found in a drainage ditch with two bodies inside, a fingertip torn from a latex glove would point investigators to both the crime scene and the killer.
A three-year-old develops a respiratory condition. His father has Alzheimers.

It was one of the most brazen crimes of the 20th century. Adolph Coors III, chairman of the Coors Brewing Company, was kidnapped and held for ransom. The crime prompted one of the most intense manhunts in United States history.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica.

A suspicious fire sweeps through an apartment, killing two young women. The cause of the fire and the identity of the victims are unclear, but a closer look at the scene reveals something hidden in the ashes.
An examination of the 2002 DC area shooting spree that resulted in ten murders.
A woman convicted of killing her mother in a car fire is granted a new trial.
Even though their daughter had run away before, she had always come back. Her parents were sure this time would be no different, but they were wrong.
Notepad points to kidnapper.
When a dry cleaner employee is raped and murdered in her store, police turn to forensic science for the answers they need.
Debate over cause of death.

A woman was found dead on the bedroom floor of her apartment. The crime scene yielded little of value and investigators wondered if they would find enough evidence to make a case, much less catch a killer.
A killer leaves the scene with the genetic fingerprint of his victim.
When a college student is found dead, evidence suggests that he knew his killer. With just three hairs and some microscopic cells, police unravel a web of lies and find the motive for murder.
A vacuum-cleaner bag of microscopic paint-particles helps to identify a killer.
Doctors don't know why a young scientist has fallen gravely ill. When tests finally reveal the cause, it's too late to save him.
A mother of two vanishes after a shopping trip. Her body is discovered a month later.
The 1996 investigation into 48-year-old Martha Hansen's murder is helped by a legal requirement that bars have video cameras installed on the premises.
A physics professor and NASA technology help to catch a killer.
After being admitted to the hospital with unexplained bleeding, 11-month-old Chad Shelton dies. Investigators and scientists frantically search for a cause when others from the same house fall ill.
In 1993, worldwide attention focused on robberies which targeted tourists in Florida.

In 1993, the Amtrak Railroad experienced the deadliest train crash in United States history when the Sunset Limited derailed while crossing Alabama's Big Bayou Canot bridge. 47 passengers and crew were killed; scores more were injured.
At a murder scene, investigators find a shoe-print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints.
In 2001, Ginger Hayes and her infant son were abducted during a carjacking. The crime had been reported by a witness within minutes of occurrence.
A death in Pennsylvania is strikingly similar to one in North Carolina.
Police investigate a missing college girl and discover her double life: attending school by day and working as a call-girl by night. Her body is found and investigators find her killer.
A nurse learns that she has been deliberately infected with HIV.
Sometime during a neighborhood Christmas party, five-year-old Melissa Brannen disappeared. Investigators turned to forensic science to help them see what the witnesses missed.
A pregnant woman is found murdered in her air-conditioned bedroom.

It was supposed to be a routine motorcade for the Queen of England. But on the way to Yosemite National Park, a car carrying three Secret Service agents collided with a car driven by a deputy from the local sheriff's office.
Police were puzzled by an obscure print found at a murder crime scene.

When an 11-year-old girl disappears from a remote Alaska town, investigators wonder if she has been attacked by a bear or become lost in the dense woods. Eventually, they realize that neither assumption is true.
A man is found dead in his home and his ex-wife has an almost perfect alibi.
Prompted by news of a flight attendant's brutal murder, the son of a previous victim contacts police. Both murders have similar MOs, and biological evidence proves that these were serial killings.
A union official is executed in his home not long after a strike by the union membership.

When a college student is reported missing, police believe their investigation will be like countless others. But when they discover blood spatter in her boyfriend's bedroom, they know this case is going to be different.
In 1988, the body of a young woman was discovered in an Ohio river.
Crystal Faye Todd's case is examined; the popular high school student was raped and murdered.
In 2003, Tiffany Rowell and three of her friends were brutally murdered in affluent Clear Lake, Texas.
Police discovered the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife.

A woman was brutally murdered in her home and the only witnesses to the crime were the family dogs. An expert in canine behavior was convinced the killer knew both the victim and the animals, and he was determined find out what the dogs had seen.
More than 700 Oregonians contracted food poisoning from a unique strain of salmonella in 1984.

The disappearance of Philadelphia college athlete Aimee Willard is investigated after her car is found on the roadside. When her body is found, the police find unusual marks and DNA evidence that eventually lead to her killer.
A woman is found dead from a gunshot wound and police suspect her husband.
At the scene of a vicious murder, the killer went to a great deal of effort to wipe away his fingerprints and obscure his shoe impressions left when he tracked blood trails on the floor.
In 1995, the founder of American Atheists disappeared with $500,000 in gold coins.

Shortly after daybreak, a fire is started in a dumpster in Vancouver. No one sees the arsonist or the fire, which burns for hours in the deserted parking lot. But there's more than garbage in this flaming container.
Two eyewitnesses may hold the key to the death of a motorcycle gang member.
The crime scene was especially violent: a husband and wife had been shot to death in their bedroom. Was their 16-year-old daughter complicit?
In 1984, a passerby finds the torso of a woman in a cardboard box.
After 10 bodies turn up in Florida, one victim — 17-year-old Lisa McVey — is abducted but released. She leads police to the perpertrator, Bobbie Joe Long.
A victim's knowledge of forensic evidence leads police to her abductor.
In 2006, Darlene VanderGiesen received threatening emails and then disappeared. Tracking the source of the emails led police to the home of Daphne Wright, where they believe a murder was committed.
The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered among garbage.
When the body of a young woman is found under an isolated highway ramp, a unique fiber on the victim's clothing leads San Diego police straight to the most unlikely of killers.
In a 1992 murder case, the autopsy of a cremated body turns up telltale clues of foul play.
In 2000, Judy Southern arrived home from work and was shot by a gunman waiting within. Her husband arrived shortly afterwards, called emergency services and drove her to the hospital.
Forensic developments reveal new facts in the case of a man convicted of sexual assault.
When a victim is brutally murdered in his own bed, investigators find a shoe impression in the mud outside — physical evidence they hope will lead to the killer.
The murder of a couple puzzles investigators until the victims' dog leads police to the killer.

Time of death becomes pivotal after a pregnant woman is found murdered in her air-conditioned bedroom. A striking similarity between her death and an HBO movie gives examiners the clues they need to thaw out the alibi of a cold-blooded killer.
Soon after becoming pregnant, firefighter Michelle Baker's health quickly deteriorates.

A wealthy man and his wife were attacked by three masked men outside their luxurious Louisiana home. He was shot dead and she was forced to open their hidden safe. To solve the crime, police would have to find out who knew about the concealed safe.
In the 1980s, a trio of unsolved murders occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas.

When hunters reported finding a skull in a Texas canyon, police immediately began an investigation. With a forensic artist's reconstruction, police eventually learned the victim's identity. Now all they had to do was find her killer.
An abandoned, still-running car leads investigators to a body with unusual marks.
One warm summer afternoon, the town of Verona, Wisconsin faced its first triple homicide. To solve the case, investigators had to delve into the world of high rollers and offshore betting.
Police uncover deleted computer files during an investigation.
In 1996, Indiana police identified Richard Alexander as the “River Park Rapist” who assaulted four women that year. Later, DNA analysis casts doubt on his conviction.
A suspicious neighbor gives police a break in a cold case.
It would take 46 years, handwriting analysis and new fingerprint technology to solve the 1957 murders of two California police officers.
The 1987 disappearance of Houston resident Tracy Jo Shine is recalled.
In 1989, the dead bodies of Joan Rogers and her two teenage daughters were found floating in Tampa Bay.
Doctors cannot pinpoint the source of a businessman's illness.
On the night of May 22, 1992, Betty Wilson returned home after a meeting and discovered her husband lying in a pool of blood. Jack Wilson had obviously been murdered — but how?
After 6-year-old Michelle Lee Dorr went missing, her father confessed to murdering her.

Seattle police had no suspects in the violent murder of grunge singer Mia Zapata. More than a decade passed before evidence collected by a prescient medical examiner could be used by forensic scientists to identify the killer.
The 1996 investigation into 48-year-old Martha Hansen's murder is helped by a legal requirement.

Susie Mowbray was charged in her husband's death. Her son was so convinced of her innocence that he enrolled in law school, studied all of the evidence and, eventually, discovered the truth of what really happened between his parents.
The disappearance of a mail-order bride is suspicious when police learn of the husband's past wives.
Two sets of scientists probe a woman's death.
